title: Around Bethesda's Healing Wave
description: Around Bethesda's Healing Wave in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Bernard Barton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 221 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Pool of Bethesda”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-round Be-thes-da's heal-ing wave Wait-ing to hear the rust-ling wing, Which spoke the an-gel nigh, who gave Its vir-tue to that ho-ly spring, With pa-tience, and with hope en-dued Were seen the ga-thered mul-ti-tude.

lines: Waiting to hear the rustling wing,
Which spoke the angel nigh, who gave
Its virtue to that holy spring,
With patience, and with hope endued
Had they who watched and waited there
Been conscious who was passing by,
Would they have sought his pitying eye;
And craved with fervency of soul,
His Power Divine to make them whole!
Bethesda's pool has lost its power!
No angel, by his glad descent,
Which with its healing waters went.
But he, whose word surpassed its wave,

licence: Public domain: Bernard Barton died in 1849.
credits: Words by Bernard Barton (1784–1849), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
